title: Weighed recipes: chin chin, puff-puff, meat pie and bread

say: Weighed recipes: chin chin, puff-puff, meat pie and bread.
This is the video for module two of Basic Baking and Snacks Production.
Professional bakers weigh. A cup of flour can weigh anywhere from about 120 g to 160 g, depending on how you scoop it.

say: Drain on paper and let it cool completely before you pack it in airtight bags. Too much flour or too little fat makes it rock hard.

say: For puff-puff, beat 500 g of flour, sugar, salt and one 7 g sachet of yeast with lukewarm water for 3 to 5 minutes. Cover it in a warm place for 45 to 60 minutes, until doubled and bubbly.
Fry small balls at about 170 to 180 degrees, and serve the same day.
Do not crowd the pot. Each piece cools the oil, and the snack soaks up oil. For example, Ngozi fries her double batch about 10 at a time. Never leave hot oil unattended.
Meat pie sells at a higher price. Cook the minced beef and onion until no pink remains, then add potatoes and carrots.

say: Thicken it with flour and water, spread it on a tray to cool, and refrigerate it if you will not use it within 2 hours.

say: For the pastry, use 500 g of flour and 250 g of cold margarine. The fat is half the flour weight.

say: Rub in the fat and add cold water. Do not knead, or the pastry turns hard. Chill the dough for about 20 minutes.

say: Fill with cold filling, seal with a fork, brush with egg, and bake at about 180 to 200 degrees for 25 to 35 minutes, until the base is golden.
Hot filling makes a soggy base, and raw meat may not reach a safe temperature in the oven.

say: For example, Hauwa in Kaduna gets an order for 60 meat pies. Her recipe makes 12.
She finds one factor: 60 divided by 12 is 5.
She multiplies every ingredient by 5. Flour, 500 g times 5, is 2,500 g. Margarine is 1,250 g.
She adds about 10% extra to cover breakages and a tasting sample.
And she mixes in two or three smaller batches, because a huge batch warms up and is hard to rub in evenly.
Bread shows every step. Knead for 10 to 15 minutes, until a small piece stretches thin enough to let light through. That is the windowpane test.

panel.heading: Improve one batch at a time
items: Bake a loaf; windowpane test the dough

say: For example, Grace in Port Harcourt bakes her first loaf. Her four tasters score texture 2 out of 5. Heavy and tight. Her notes show she kneaded for only 5 minutes.

items: Bake a loaf; windowpane test the dough

say: She changes one thing only. She kneads for 12 minutes, with a windowpane test.

panel.rule: Change only one thing per bake

say: Texture rises to 3.5. Now tasters say it is a little pale.

say: Next time she bakes 5 minutes longer, and appearance rises from 3 to 4. One change at a time shows what worked.

say: So remember. Weigh everything in grams. Cool chin chin fully before packing. Fry in small batches at the right temperature.
Cook the meat filling fully and cool it before filling. And scale every recipe with one factor.

panel.heading: Key points
items: Cool chin chin fully before packing
Fry in small batches at the right heat
Cook and cool meat pie filling first

say: Your practice: fry and record one batch, bake meat pies or a pound cake, write a recipe scaled for 50 pieces, and run a tasting panel.
